supersedes: E1_cert_vs_truth.json (spec hash 1eaa62eba4ae...), withdrawn 2026-10-24. The earlier run did not estimate anything from fresh data: it read archived results and used hard-coded and invented intervals, and its design compared quantities in different units (class positions versus flow kernels). Its results are withdrawn and are not reported.
question: On the same fresh data, is certifying the summed response (a linear functional of the merged measure) at least an order of magnitude cheaper than identifying the agents' memories, as the thesis predicts?
data: Binance USD-M perpetual futures daily archives (data.binance.vision): 1-minute klines (close, quote volume, taker-buy quote volume) and 5-minute metrics (sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio, count_toptrader_long_short_ratio, count_long_short_ratio). Every file is checked against Binance's .CHECKSUM and its SHA-256 is logged.
dates_rule: the 4th, 5th, 18th, 19th and 23rd of every month from 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-30 (105 dates)
freshness: A scan of every result file, notebook and script in the repository that mentions any of these symbols finds no 2025-2026 date on the 4th, 5th, 18th, 19th or 23rd of a month; the day-of-month sets used before are (10, 24), (6, 20), (3, 17), (2, 9), 22, (11, 12), (13, 14), (25-28) and others listed in thesis/evidence/E1v2_freshness.json.

estimators.returns_and_flow: five-minute log returns (bp) and signed taker flow ($M) at the five-minute marks where class ratios are published (Paper 1, Part 6 code)
estimators.certificate: OLS of five-minute flow on 12 lagged five-minute returns, pooled over days with day-demeaning; Phi_hat = sum of the 12 coefficients
estimators.price_only_memories: two exponentials fitted to the 12-tap kernel by least squares (rates in [0, 0.99], four starts); r_fast < r_slow; Delta r = r_slow - r_fast
estimators.class_tagged_memories: for each of three classes, OLS of n_t on (n_{t-1}, ret_t), n = (R-1)/(R+1), day-demeaned
estimators.intervals: day-bootstrap percentile 95% intervals, 200 draws, seed 20261024 + symbol index

per_symbol.I_id: width of the Delta r interval / |Delta r_hat|
per_symbol.P2_holds: mean width of the two price-only rate intervals >= 10 * mean width of the three class-tagged rate intervals

primary_1: P1 holds in at least 75% of evaluable symbols, and its Holm-adjusted one-sided binomial p-value (null rate 1/2) is below 0.05.
primary_2: P2 holds in at least 75% of evaluable symbols, and its Holm-adjusted one-sided binomial p-value (null rate 1/2) is below 0.05.
correction: Holm across the two primaries at level 0.05.
evaluable: a symbol is evaluable with at least 30 valid days (at least 100 five-minute marks with class ratios); the test is void if fewer than 20 symbols are evaluable.
secondary: number of symbols whose Phi interval excludes zero (Paper 1's part (iii) on new days)
number of symbols whose top-position and all-account rates differ
median I_cert, median I_id, median width ratio
prior_information: Paper 1's registered test on 42 earlier fresh days found price-only rate intervals 27.6 to 124 times wider than tagged ones in 30 of 30 symbols (relevant to P2), and Phi significantly different from zero in only 5 of 30 symbols (relevant to P1). P2 is therefore a replication on new days; P1 is a new, risky prediction that can fail if Phi is not precisely estimated from passive data.
interpretation: A pass of P1 supports the thesis's claim that certification is cheaper than identification in real passive data. A fail of P1 means that, from passive five-minute data in these markets, the certificate is not an order of magnitude more precise than memory separation; it would not contradict the theorems, which concern controlled experiments, but it would limit the empirical claim, and it will be reported as a failure.
opening_rule: The specification, its hash and an unlock counter at 0 are committed and pushed to origin/main in a commit of their own, before any of these files is downloaded. The pipeline refuses to run unless the committed specification matches its hash and the counter is 0; it sets the counter to 1, downloads the data and evaluates once. The counter, results, numbers and download log are then committed together.
